candidates.rationale: Biallelic inactivation occurs in about 80-90% of ccRCC (mutation, deletion or methylation), driving constitutive HIF stabilization and defining the disease's core dependency.

HIF-2α is the key oncogenic driver downstream of VHL loss, and the inhibitor belzutifan produced about 49% ORR in VHL-disease RCC and improved PFS and ORR in pretreated advanced ccRCC (LITESPARK-005).
HIF-driven VEGF underlies the hypervascular phenotype, and VEGF/VEGFR blockade (bevacizumab, sunitinib, axitinib, cabozantinib) is the long-standing backbone of therapy.
VEGFR2 is the main target of TKIs such as axitinib, sunitinib, pazopanib, lenvatinib and cabozantinib, which give ORR around 25-55% in the first line, especially in combinations.
PD-L1 and PD-1 blockade (nivolumab, pembrolizumab) improves overall survival in combinations, but PD-L1 expression is only weakly predictive of benefit in ccRCC.

Truncating mutations occur in about 40% of ccRCC and are associated with response to anti-angiogenic therapy (IMmotion150) and with possible resistance to ICI in some cohorts, though results are inconsistent.
Mutated in about 10-15% of ccRCC, BAP1 loss is associated with high grade and worse survival and is mutually exclusive with PBRM1 loss.
Mutated in about 10-15% of ccRCC, SETD2 loss is associated with H3K36me3 depletion, genomic instability and poorer outcomes, and may confer vulnerability to WEE1 inhibition.

A HIF target expressed in more than 90% of ccRCC, CAIX is a diagnostic and imaging marker (girentuximab PET/CT, with about 85% sensitivity and 87% specificity in ZIRCON) and a therapeutic antibody target.
MET is a target of cabozantinib, which improved PFS and OS versus everolimus (METEOR) and is also part of the combinations with nivolumab (CheckMate 9ER) and pembrolizumab/lenvatinib.
